ExpandR: Yao et al. [20] approach the problem in the perspective of retrieval side. Retrieval augmented generation is that concept: prior to the generation of an answer, one should seek out some relevant documents and serve as grounding. However, on most RAG systems the retriever and generator are attached by way of a bolt, but they are not very well synchronized. ExpandR approaches this problem differently, optimizing the two together. The LLM is conditioned to generate query expansions with which the retriever can realistically work on and the retriever is conditioned to retrieve documents which the LLM can actually use. They do this joint optimization using Direct Preference Optimization, whose reward function is to compromise quality of retrievals with consistency of generation.
